title: Facts of 7, 8 and 9
short: Learn the hardest facts with patterns and break-apart strategies.

blocks.html: These are the facts people find hardest, but you already have the tools. Breaking apart and doubling handle every one of them.

9 groups is one group less than 10 groups, so take one group away from the 10s fact. 8 groups is two sets of 4 groups, so double the 4s fact. 7 groups is 5 groups and 2 groups. Each strategy just splits or adjusts the groups, so the total is right.

blocks.name: hundredchart
blocks.cap: The 9s march down and to the left: each is 10 more, minus 1. Their digits always add to 9 (up to 90).

blocks.html: Nines: ten groups minus one. Eights: double the fours. Sevens: five groups plus two groups.
Taking away the wrong number in the 9s. $9 \times 6$ is ten 6s minus one 6: $60 - 6 = 54$. Taking away 9 gives 51, which is wrong. The digit check catches it: $5 + 1 = 6$, not 9.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Grade 3, 3.OA.C.7 (by the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers)
